_comment: Full 'same condition as SHADeS' HK training in one job: full 16,976-image Hyper-Kvasir train split, 20 epochs (matching the paper's recipe, arXiv:2502.12994, and matching weights_19 in the baseline SHADeS checkpoint name -- epoch indices are 0-based, so weights_19 is the final epoch, matching the baseline's naming). Trained on HK only (C3VD held out for eval only), fresh start (no load_weights_folder, same initialization point as v_tau050) for a fair comparison against the HK-pretrained SHADeS baseline. On GPU (Quadro RTX 6000 x4). save_frequency=1 so a disconnect never loses more than one epoch of progress. noadjust=true to match the real baseline checkpoint name (ckpt/finetuned_mono_hkfull_288_pseudo_dsms_automasking_noadjust) -- fixed from an earlier version of this config that had noadjust=false, which does not match the baseline and (after the Oct-3 commit's crash-fix for that code path was reverted) would crash on epoch 0.
_loss_weights_comment: Kept identical to every other SHADeS++ run this session rather than guessing a mapping onto the paper's (lambda_d, lambda_a, lambda_r, lambda_es) notation -- this code has more loss terms than the paper's summary describes, so there's no verified 1:1 correspondence, and reflec_constraint is confirmed dead code (unused in trainer.py, like tau).
